horā
(‘astrology’)
------------------------------------------
This word seems to have been borrowed from the greek ‘hora’ and was used for the first time by वराहमिहिर (6th century A. D.).
Hindu अस्त्रोलोग्य् (jyotiṣa) includes three skandhas or branches: tantra (determination of the motions of प्लनेत्स्), होरा (jātaka or होरोस्चोपे) and śākhā (various kinds of divinations).
A work that embodies all these three is called ‘saṁhitā’.
Horā has two other meanings in अस्त्रोलोग्य्: lagna (that sign which is rising on the eastern horizon at the particular moment) and half of a राशि (zodiacal sign).
See also JYOTIṢA.
